correctness.rationale: Use the conjugate of the polynomial coefficient vector in the Hermitian lift v(z)*Hv(z). The six-point DFT separates modes 0, ±1 and ±2 and combines ±3 into one real Nyquist equation per ring. When sin(3(ψ−φ))≠0 the two Nyquist equations kill h03. At distinct a=r² and b=s² the second-superdiagonal linear coefficient polynomial vanishes identically; the first-superdiagonal quadratic is c(t−a)(t−b), and the diagonal cubic is (t−a)(t−b)(u+vt). This characterizes the entire kernel and gives real dimension four. If c≠0 the three adjacent entries are nonzero and the tridiagonal recurrence shows nullity at most one. If c=0, a nonzero diagonal polynomial cannot have at most two monomials and two distinct positive roots. Hence no nonzero difference of two rank-one lifts can lie in the kernel. For equal radii, 1 and (z/r)^3 have equal sampled moduli; for angular resonance e^(−3iφ)z³ is real at every node and 1±i e^(−3iφ)z³ are an ambiguity. These witnesses are inequivalent, and the lift covers zero and lower degrees. claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: At d=3 each lower harmonic divided by its radius power must vanish at the two squared radii. Degree one then vanishes, degree two has one complex free multiplier and degree three on the real diagonal has two real free coefficients, yielding exactly the displayed kernel by factorization. Injectivity already rules out indefinite rank-two lifts, and a nonzero semidefinite lift cannot vanish on the spanning evaluation vectors. Thus the rank exclusion follows without a new theorem. Derivative measurements do not imply this geometry.
